title: TypeScript SDK codegen for polymorphic shape mappers and Zod hydrators (streaming examples)
creator: Ravi Shah
description:
Problem: We need a robust, low-friction way for customers to surface structured output from the TypeScript SDK when models return polymorphic objects across streaming and non-streaming responses. Current ad-hoc patterns require users to write repetitive runtime guards and manual stitching logic for streamed fragments.

Goal: Ship a codegen + runtime helper suite that produces: (1) type-safe mappers for polymorphic shapes, (2) Zod schema hydrators that upgrade plain JSON into typed runtime-validated objects, and (3) streaming helpers that assemble fragmentary outputs and run incremental validation without blocking token-level streaming. Must integrate with existing tsdk streaming APIs and align with output-contracts testing harness.
acceptance_criteria: CLI codegen generates TypeScript union mappers and Zod schemas for a given JSON-schema input
Generated runtime exposes `isX()` type guards and `hydrateX()` helpers that restore prototypes and attach helper methods
Streaming path supports incremental fragment stitching and runs partial validators with deterministic reconciliation when trailing tokens arrive
Docs and two end-to-end examples (chat + rerank) included in SDK examples folder
Unit tests cover generated guards, hydrate APIs, and streaming assembly edge cases (out-of-order fragments, truncated tokens)
proposed_solution:
Add a new codegen target `tsdk:hydrator` that consumes a JSON Schema or ts-sdk shape descriptor and emits: 1) Zod schemas with discriminators configured, 2) lightweight runtime validators (fast path) plus full validators (Zod) (configurable), and 3) streaming helper module that maintains a fragment buffer keyed by `fragmentId` and runs incremental shape checks on the buffer prefix.

Design notes: Use a schema fingerprint in the header so runtime can detect mismatches and fall back to permissive decoding. For discriminators, prefer explicit `type` tag resolution but also support multi-field tag inference. Hydrators should be tree-shakable and support a `hydrate(obj, opts)` that can attach class prototypes (e.g., Message, Choice) without requiring users to import classes manually.
technical_notes: Runtime will include two guard flavors: `fastGuard` (generated predicate) and `zodGuard` (zod.safeParse). Use fastGuard for streaming prefix checks to avoid expensive parsing.

Streaming helper will expose `createFragmentAssembler({onComplete, onPartial})` which accepts fragment payloads and emits reassembled JSON when complete or periodic partials for optimistic UI updates.
Codegen will emit example signatures: `isChoice(x): x is Choice`, `hydrateChoice(x): Choice` and `ChoiceSchema` (Zod).
Schema fingerprint: sha1(jsonSchema) to allow runtime mismatch telemetry and automatic compatibility mode (permissive).
Performance target: generated guards should validate common discriminators in < 1us on 2k element payloads (microbenchmark target).
tasks: Write codegen plugin that maps JSON-schema discriminator to union TS types and Zod unions
Implement runtime `hydrate` utilities and prototype reattachment helpers
Add streaming fragment assembler + incremental validator integration into tsdk stream consumer
Create two example apps: `chat-polymorphic-output` and `rerank-streaming-hydrate` in examples/
Add unit and integration tests; plug generated artifacts into output-contracts test harness
Create docs + migration guide for teams using manual guards
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed—validated approach of emitting both fast predicates and Zod schema. Microbenchmarks show fastGuard 5-8x faster than zod.safeParse for shallow discriminators.
2026-02-20: Initial codegen prototype can emit union types and Zod unions from a sample schema. Generated `isFoo` signatures type-check correctly in sample repo.
2026-02-28: Streaming fragment assembler design reviewed with infra; decided to keep assembler state in-memory per StreamContext with optional persistence hook for long-running streams.
2026-03-05: PR #1489 opened with hydrate utilities and unit tests for prototype reattachment. Seeking design review for attachable prototypes pattern.
2026-03-12: Implemented optimistic partial validation using `fastGuard` on prefixes; second pass converts to full zod validation on completion. Integration tests in progress.
review_comments: PM (Leah Kim): Prefer conservative defaults — streaming should not throw on partial mismatch; use telemetry to surface mismatches instead of failing requests.
Design (Marco): Example UX should highlight `hydrate()` benefits for IDE auto-complete (methods restored) to convince product teams to adopt hydrators.
Security (Priya Desai): Ensure hydrators cannot cause prototype pollution; performance review suggested explicit allowlist for attachable prototypes.
Infra (Jon Park): For Dedicated customers, ensure fingerprint telemetry is opt-out and does not leak PII.
followups: Add generator target to SDK CI and autopublish artifacts to npm under @redwood/tsdk-hydrators
Explore a Python SDK counterpart (hydrate into dataclasses) as a follow-up epics
Monitor telemetry for schema fingerprint mismatches and add migration tooling if needed
